newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Sept 17.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
ACTION AT LAST ON DANGER MEN

The Health Secretary Stephen Dorrell is to announce the withdrawal of hospital managers' rights to discharge mental patients into the community. The controversial loophole has led to some tragic blunders, in which dangerous mental patients have been freed and have then committed attacks and rapes.

The Alliance & Leicester ALL.CN building society, which is in the process of converting into a bank, lent 47 percent less to homebuyers in the first half of this year compared to the same period last year. However, pre-tax profits for the six months to June increased by 12 percent on 1995's figures. This pattern is shared with the Halifax, whose gross lending fell from 6.6 billion stg to 4.8 billion stg.
JOBS THREAT TOPS AGENDA AT SUMMIT
The Franco-German summit will be dominated by discussion of the threat to meeting the criteria for monetary union posed by rising unemployment.
AMERICAN STEPS UP BA DEAL PRESSURE
Bob Crandall, president of American Airlines, will meet with Deputy Prime Minister Michael Heseltine today to request government support for the alliance with British Airways.
RIVALS ON THE HOP AS TESCO TACTICS FORCE PACE

Sir Ian MacLaurin's pledge as chief executive of Tesco to sell the cheapest goods of all leading supermarkets and his introduction of the innovative Clubcard, have achieved market leadership for the store. Tesco is now investing 30 million stg in a new "Unbeatable Value" campaign, which promises to match the cheapest price on 600 products.
P&O SOUNDS OUT STENA FOR LINK-UP
P&O is engaged in high-level talks with rival Stena Line, with a view to pooling resources to meet the challenge of the Channel Tunnel.
